match.reason: No bank point teaches how natural processes such as weather, erosion, fire, floods and plate movement change environments over time; the closest, geo-natural-hazards, is about when a process threatens people, and the others cover interconnection and the general definition of environment.

draft.title: Natural processes that change environments
card: Natural processes happen without people causing them. They change environments, sometimes slowly over thousands of years and sometimes in a few hours.
Weather and erosion
Wind, rain and waves wear away rock and soil and carry it elsewhere. Over time this can shape valleys, gullies and coastlines.
Fire and floods
Bushfires can burn away plants and change which species grow back. Floods spread water and sediment over land, and can reshape river channels.
Plate movement
Earth's plates move slowly and can cause earthquakes, volcanoes and the building of mountains. A sudden event such as an eruption can change a landscape quickly.
draft.remember: Natural processes, from slow erosion to sudden floods, fires and plate movement, change environments with no human cause.

a.q: Which of these is an example of a natural process changing an environment?
opts: Floodwater reshaping the channel of a river
A farmer clearing bushland for crops
A town building a dam across a creek
A factory releasing smoke into the air
a.why: A flood is a natural process that can reshape a river channel without any human cause. The other three are actions by people, so they are not natural processes.
a.clue: Which change would still happen if no people were involved?

b.q: Waves along a sandstone coast near Port Macquarie slowly wear back the cliffs over hundreds of years. Which process is changing this coast?
opts: Erosion
Plate movement
Bushfire
Flooding
b.why: Waves wearing away rock and carrying material elsewhere is erosion. Plate movement works by moving Earth's crust, such as in earthquakes, not by waves wearing rock away.
b.clue: What do waves do to rock over a long time?

a.best: Floodwater reshaping the channel of a river

problems.detail: The coast near Port Macquarie is not a sandstone coast. Its rocky headlands are mostly older rocks such as serpentinite, basalt and metamorphic rock, while sandstone cliffs are typical of the Sydney region. Name a place with sandstone cliffs (such as Sydney's coast) or drop 'sandstone'.
